summary.text: Julie Fedorchak is the Republican incumbent for North Dakota's at-large House seat, first elected in 2024. A communications professional who worked in state government and ran her own communications business, she served on the North Dakota Public Service Commission from 2013 to 2025. She sits on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, and her official issues pages focus on energy, agriculture, and the budget.

paragraphs.text: Fedorchak was born in Williston, North Dakota, and raised in Fargo, the youngest of eight children; she graduated from Bismarck Century High School and describes herself as a fourth-generation North Dakotan.
She earned a B.A. in journalism from the University of North Dakota in 1991 and began her career as a communications and media relations specialist.
From 1995 to 2000 she was a spokesperson for Gov. Ed Schafer (R); her official biography describes the role as communications director.
Fedorchak then founded a communications business that she says she ran for 10 years, working with clients in business, government, and politics and authoring several books and articles.
In 2011 she became North Dakota state director for U.S. Sen. John Hoeven (R).
Gov. Jack Dalrymple appointed Fedorchak to the North Dakota Public Service Commission in November 2012; she was sworn in on January 2, 2013, and served until 2025.

During that time she served as president of the National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners (NARUC), a post her official biography says ended in November 2024, and as president of the Organization of MISO States (OMS).
In the 2024 general election Fedorchak won North Dakota's at-large House seat with 69.2% of the vote over Trygve Hammer, succeeding Kelly Armstrong, and took office on January 3, 2025.
In the 2025-2026 Congress she serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, including its Communications and Technology, Energy, and Environment subcommittees.
She won the June 9, 2026 Republican primary with 72.8% of the vote over Alex Balazs.
According to her official biography, she lives in Mandan with her husband, Mike, and serves on the Board of Trustees of the University of Mary.
